clue.text: Drink can go cold when put back

indicators.note: put back tells us the whole run of can, go and the cold abbreviation is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap; that the letters also run backwards across can go cold is a coincidence of this charade

explanation.surface: A can of something left out goes cold when it is shoved back on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when put back' turns the whole string CANGOC round, giving the brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, so it is a kind of spirit one would drink.

clue.text: From nincompoop a question is difficult to understand

indicators.note: From says the letters are taken out of the run of words nincompoop a question

explanation.surface: Any question asked by a fool turns out to be hard to make sense of.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque writing is obscure, hard to see through, so the word means not clear to the mind.

clue.text: Broadcast end enthrals a nation

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters of end and enthrals are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The final episode of a broadcast holds a whole country spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a European country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Early type of man found in Europe scattered among corn

definitions.text: Early type of man found in Europe

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of among and corn are thrown about and settle in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remains of a prehistoric European have been found strewn through a field of corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' looks like a link word placing the man in the corn, but it is part of the fodder with 'corn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon people were early modern humans known from fossils first found in France.

clue.text: Disordered mixture? Change one letter in word game

indicators.note: this phrase tells us one letter of the game's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Scrabble is the board game of building words from letter tiles

explanation.surface: A muddled jumble of tiles, and you need to change only one to make a word in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: One B of SCRABBLE becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a confused, disorderly mix, like scrambled eggs stirred together.

clue.text: Delay money paid out around America

indicators.note: around says the money word wraps itself about the abbreviation for America

parts.note: a spend is an amount of money laid out
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: Payment is held back while money is sent out round the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off for a time, a synonym for deferring it.

clue.text: Gather outside clubs to look back on S past things

definitions.text: look back on S past things

indicators.note: outside means the gathering word sits around the card-suit letter

parts.note: to reap a crop is to gather it in
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Collecting outside the golf clubhouse, members reminisce about old times.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'S' in the clue as held is an OCR blemish and takes no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again what has gone before, reviewing earlier points.

clue.text: Spoil is mostly rich soil

indicators.note: mostly means most of the soil word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: marl is a fertile clay-and-lime soil

explanation.surface: Fertile ground is mostly ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or blemish it, a synonym of spoil.

clue.text: Fail to take holiday abroad

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
out and abroad both mean away from home, out and about

explanation.surface: Someone fails to book their holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, failing to include or take it.

clue.text: Chary of tending to find fault with university for pressure

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in the place of another in the fault-finding word

parts.note: captious means inclined to carp and find fault
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone wary of nit-picking critics at university under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with university for pressure': U replaces P in CAPTIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chary means wary and careful, which is what cautious means too.

clue.text: Pen for livestock arriving back through mountain pass

indicators.note: through means the turned word runs inside the mountain-pass word

parts.note: col is a pass or saddle between peaks

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for arriving is written right to left

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arriving

explanation.surface: Animals come back to their pen through a pass in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ARR into RRA, which goes 'through' COL.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for horses or cattle, a pen for keeping livestock.

clue.text: Triumphant cry of Greek getting European perks, as regularly given

parts.note: Eur. is an abbreviation for European

indicators.note: regularly given means every other letter of perks and as is taken

explanation.surface: A Greek is jubilant at getting European Union benefits handed out on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly given' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'perks, as': E, K, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes is said to have shouted this Greek word, meaning I have found it, so it is a cry of triumph.

clue.text: One making foreign sales right after exhibition attended by Queen

indicators.note: after places the right abbreviation behind the exhibition word
attended by puts the queen's letters alongside, at the end

parts.note: expo is short for exposition, a large exhibition
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A trader making overseas deals turns up right after the trade show, which the Queen visits.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter is a business or person selling goods to buyers abroad.

clue.text: Wagner epic has a harsh critic — though nuts are totally engaged with it

definitions.text: nuts are totally engaged with it

parts.note: Wagner's Ring cycle is his four-opera epic
has contracts to 's, giving an S
a panner is a reviewer who pans, slates, what they see

explanation.surface: The Ring is mauled by a savage reviewer, though fanatics are utterly gripped by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the fans of the surface; it is the threaded hardware, which a closed-ended wrench encircles completely.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring spanner has a closed ring end that fits right round a nut, gripping it on every side.

clue.text: Unduly prolonged? Groan wouldn't go amiss

indicators.note: go amiss means the letters of groan and wouldn't go wrong and end up rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Asked whether something went on too long, one says a groan would not be out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-drawn-out has been dragged on for far longer than needed.

clue.text: Saucy line he's put into play?

definitions.text: Saucy line he's put into play?

indicators.note: put into play means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A dramatist slips a cheeky line into his script.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the Greek tragedian could be said to put a line into each play.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus was the ancient Athenian tragedian who wrote plays such as the Oresteia.

clue.text: Medicine needs to be prompt that's swallowed right at four

indicators.note: swallowed means the following letters go inside the prompt word

parts.note: a cue is a prompt to an actor
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Medicine has to be taken promptly, swallowed right at four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A curative is a remedy, a medicine that heals or cures.

clue.text: Jogging takes its toll; ready to keep going?

parts.note: jogging is slow running
a thing that costs exacts a price, takes its toll

explanation.surface: Exercise wears a runner down; are they fit enough to carry on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like 'prepared'; it is the slang noun for cash, which keeps a business going.
explanation.definitionFit: Running costs are the everyday money spent to keep a car or business going; ready is slang for cash.

clue.text: Artwork featuring headless parrot The Tim inside wire bars

indicators.note: inside means the beheaded bird goes within the barred enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure of wire bars

indicators.note: headless means the parrot word loses its first letter

parts.note: Poll, Polly, is a traditional name for a parrot

explanation.surface: A piece of art shows a parrot with no head inside a wire cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tim' in the clue as held is OCR debris and takes no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is an artwork made by sticking assorted materials onto a backing.

clue.text: English arriving in very pleasant Adriatic city

indicators.note: arriving in means the English letter enters the following pair of words

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: An Englishman arrives in a very pleasant city on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the canal city at the head of the Adriatic Sea in Italy.

clue.text: Rap fails to be represented as music drama

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters of rap and fails take a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rap music falls flat when staged as an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera, which he styled a sacred festival drama.

clue.text: Entrance hall for bringing in the old Call 087

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for encloses the old form of the

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A lobby that welcomes the old folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call 087' in the clue as held is OCR debris and takes no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the entrance lobby of a theatre, hotel or house.

clue.text: Bliss variation's ending on rhythmic rise and fall

indicators.note: on means the letter is placed after the next word in the answer

parts.note: the heave of the sea or a chest is its rhythmic rise and fall

indicators.note: ending means only the final letter of variation is used

explanation.surface: Pure joy at the closing variation in a piece with a swelling rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is a state of supreme happiness, so it means bliss.

clue.text: Term for a girl or boy

definitions.meaning: a name for the spring term at Oxford, Dublin and the law courts
a first name given to both women and men

explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is both the name of a university term and a first name used for either sex.

clue.text: Answer I would support

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Whatever the answer, I would back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid is to help or support someone, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fabulous place down-under?

parts.note: a fabulous place is one from fable; down under means not Australia but sunk beneath the waves

explanation.surface: A dream destination in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down-under' suggests Australia; the mythical land lies beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island that sank beneath the ocean, a mythical lost land.

clue.text: General first to march in to challenge policeman

indicators.note: in means the first letter of march goes inside the challenge word

parts.note: to dare someone is to challenge them

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of march is used

explanation.surface: A general is first to march in and confront a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police, a policeman.

clue.text: Carriage headed off by Henry

definitions.meaning: Henry Howard, Earl with this title, poet, was beheaded under Henry VIII in 1547

explanation.definitionFit: A surrey is a light carriage, and the Earl of that county-title was executed by Henry VIII.
